pages.page_summary: This page contains exercises 5.1, 5.2, and 5.3 from a Physics textbook. Exercise 5.1 asks to determine the sign of work done in various scenarios. Exercise 5.2 involves calculating work done by applied force, friction, and net force on a moving body. Exercise 5.3 refers to Figure 5.11, which displays four different potential energy functions V(x) in one dimension, and asks to identify regions where a particle cannot be found for a given total energy E.
knowledge_points: Exercise 5.1: Determine the sign (positive or negative) of work done in five specific physical scenarios: (a) lifting a bucket from a well, (b) gravitational force in that case, (c) friction on a body sliding down an inclined plane, (d) applied force on a body moving with uniform velocity on a rough horizontal plane, (e) resistive force of air on a vibrating pendulum.

Exercise 5.2: A 2 kg body moves under a 7 N horizontal force on a table with a coefficient of kinetic friction of 0.1. Calculate work done by applied force, friction, and net force in 10 seconds, and the change in kinetic energy.

Exercise 5.3: Analyze four potential energy functions V(x) shown in Fig. 5.11. For a given total energy E (indicated by a cross), specify regions where the particle cannot be found and determine the minimum total energy required in each case.
